listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, October 27. Our lead story today is Israel's election. Polls are open in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history. The campaign has been defined by security and democracy. It is the first national vote since the Hamas-led attacks of 2023 set off a chain of conflicts across the region. Netanyahu is vying for reelection. Many fear that neither of the two leading blocs will win enough seats for a majority. That could mean weeks or months of political wrangling before a government forms. Now the front page. Anthropic has filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering. That is a significant step for the company behind Claude. In Ukraine, a local ceasefire took effect in the south ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by Melania Trump. Missile attacks resumed in Kyiv. In the NBA, Alperen Sengun had twenty-nine points, nine assists and nine rebounds. The Houston Rockets stayed unbeaten with a 120 to 110 win over the Atlanta Hawks. And Science News reports that Anthropic says Claude helped a scientist plan potentially risky bird flu research. It raises questions about the role of AI in biology. Now the sections. In tech, OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra, with an emphasis on visual reasoning and computer use. A new repository from t3dotgg collects agent skills that work with Claude Code. NVIDIA's SkillSpector scans agent skills for security risks before you install them. In politics, The Lever discusses its investigation into how millions of dollars tied to the Israel lobby are being routed through other groups. Drop Site reports that Pakistan removed the country's last opposition provincial government. And the administration is trying to prosecute James Comey over what it calls a decade-old leak. His lawyers say the effort is invalid and outside the time limit. In world news, NPR has a quick guide to Israel's election. China's party plenum began Monday, about a year before Xi is expected to secure a fourth term. Jordan carried out a strike in Syria in retaliation for a church attack. In sports, the four and oh Rockets host the Bucks tonight, looking for a fifth straight win. ESPN looks at what could be next for Alexander Volkanovski after UFC 333. And Kyle Shanahan gave an injury update on Christian McCaffrey after the 49ers' game against the Falcons. In Atlanta, MARTA has begun construction on its Cleveland-Metropolitan rapid transit project. Plans are taking shape for the Atlanta Prison Farm site as a large public park. And a new residential project has topped out in Avondale Estates. In architecture, Casa 9 is a tropical retreat under a big A-frame roof. Santa Rosa Social Housing looks at housing in Santiago. And Ironwood Retreat sits beside Oak Creek in Sedona. In science, Perseverance measured Martian dust on spacesuit materials. The iceberg A-81 has reached South Georgia. And Science News looks at how volcanoes shaped human history. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Israel heads to polls for pivotal election defined by security and democracy
lead.note: Israel is voting today in what many view as one of the most pivotal elections in the country's history. The campaign has been defined by questions of security and democracy. It is the first national vote since the Hamas-led attacks of 2023 set off a chain of conflicts across the region. Netanyahu is vying for reelection as polls open. Many fear that neither of the two leading political blocs will win enough seats for a majority. If that happens, weeks or months of political wrangling may lie ahead. That means a clear winner may not emerge quickly once the votes are counted. NPR has published a quick guide to the key players, issues and when to expect a result. Readers can watch for coalition talks rather than a single election-night verdict.
